old: It is worth separating the type of similarity enforced by the matching procedure from chemical identity. A mutual nearest-neighbor relationship in 14 geometry descriptors means that each member is the closest available entry to the other in the selected standardized descriptor space. It does not mean that every pore aperture, surface atom, charge distribution, or adsorption-site orientation is identical. Indeed, the available identifiers describe different topologies and different elemental compositions for M029 and M085. This distinction is a source of scientific leverage, not a flaw: the pair asks how much chemical specificity can be concealed by geometric similarity.
new: Similarity in the nine matching descriptors does not establish chemical identity. The mutual nearest-neighbor relationship means that each member is the closest available entry to the other in that selected standardized descriptor space; it does not mean that every aperture, surface atom, charge distribution or adsorption-site orientation is identical. Identifier suffixes provide metadata labels but do not independently establish elemental composition or topology. We therefore base the pair comparison on its verified geometry coordinates and gas-resolved Henry responses, and reserve atomic or topological attribution for a structural analysis.
evidence: Nine-descriptor original matching code; CIF/atom-connectivity evidence is outside the released aggregate analysis
